answer: Seat slots are sold on a rising curve, not a flat fee: each new slot costs the base rate times the square of slots already issued, so a farm buying k seats pays a total near the cube of k. Every sale is posted on an umber board with its serial, and each slot carries one timber token that cannot be split, reused or merged, so a hundred aliases need a hundred purchases at climbing prices. A raven patrol re-reads that board each epoch and voids slots whose timber token has moved, stopping one operator from shuffling a single purchase across many seats.
